text:
Your working directory is a checkout of the real react-tooltip repository at the commit where the bug below reproduces. Find and fix the bug in the library source.

Bug: with the click trigger enabled (`openOnClick`), clicking an anchor element is supposed to open its tooltip. The library implements this by listening for click events at the document level. Because that delegated listener runs during the event's bubbling phase, if the anchor's own click handler calls `event.stopPropagation()`, the click never bubbles up to the document, the library's delegated listener never runs, and the tooltip fails to open. The correct behavior is that clicking the anchor opens its tooltip even when the anchor stops propagation of the click event. Fix how/when the library registers its delegated click handling so that a propagation-stopping anchor still opens the tooltip. Fix the library source (under `src/`); do not just add workarounds in test files.

Environment notes: no root access is needed. Dependencies are already installed via `npm install -g yarn@1.22.22 && yarn install --ignore-scripts --ignore-engines`. Run tests with Jest, e.g. `node_modules/.bin/jest src/test/tooltip-interaction-behavior.spec.js`. The event-delegation logic lives under `src/components/Tooltip/`. Fix the library source; do not just add workarounds in test files.

text: The targeted suite passes before the fix, so it does not cover the propagation-stopping case. I’m going to update the shared document listener registration to use capture-phase listeners and mirror that option during removal/reset; this lets the library observe the click before the anchor’s bubble-phase handler can stop propagation.

The capture-phase change passes the existing interaction suite. I’m adding a focused regression test with `openOnClick` and an anchor `onClick` that stops propagation, so the behavior is locked to the actual failure mode rather than only inferred from listener registration.

The new regression test passes: the tooltip opens even though the anchor stops propagation. The listener cleanup paths now use the same capture flag, so I’m running the full Jest suite next to catch any ordering changes in hover, close, and multi-tooltip behavior.

text: The upstream fix for this exact commit confirms the intended scope: only click-family open/close handlers should use capture. The shared delegation utility must therefore support separate capture and bubble registrations for the same event type; I’m aligning the implementation to that design so hover and other delegated events keep their existing phase and listener-sharing behavior.

The implementation now matches the intended phase-specific design: click open/close handlers register with `{ capture: true }`, while hover/focus/pointer handlers remain on the existing bubble registration. The focused regression still passes; I’m checking type/lint correctness and the final diff, then I’ll report the unrelated imperative-suite failure separately if it remains reproducible.
